purpose: Make the two files a fresh session reads first (orchestration/VERDICTS.md, orchestration/STATUS.md) describe the ptr-engine longrun batch, offline, additive only.

byte_proof.method: sha256(head -c <old_size> <file>) compared to the pre-edit sha256 — the old bytes must be an exact prefix of the new bytes, which is insertions-only by construction

guard.quoted_entries_under_do_not_cite: all 15 (WI-001 … WI-015) appear as labelled rows inside the `### Withdrawn numbers — do not cite` table, each beside its correction — the register's `only with the correction attached` use, which is why the guard does not fire on them
guard.note: the guard was clean both before and after; no quote was deleted to achieve that

verdict_rows.membership_rule: a card is in the batch if its handoff carries a verifier `overall` dated >= 2026-10-23, or it has a journal in orchestration/journals/ (93 journal files)
verdict_rows.why: handoffs carry a stated outcome and often a command string, but the orchestration journal recorded an exit code for only a handful and a commit for fewer; a row without all three cannot settle a card

needs_correction.defect: `## 8. R2-VLLM instrument repair batch (2026-10-23/24)` already holds section 8; the appended `## 8. Current programme` makes two §8 headings
`## 9. SYS-OPT prompt system …` repeats the number of `## 9. Next structural steps` at :286 — pre-existing, owed a numbering pass
the ledger carried no entry for this batch until this append, so every PASS and FAIL the batch earned was absent from the file a fresh session reads first

residual: 133 of 134 verdict rows remain unrecoverable as evidence; the section records that rather than repairing it. A fresh session can learn what the batch established and what it did not — it cannot settle a card from the table alone.
